narration: The framework takes two synchronized input streams over time: RGB video frames of human motion and spatial pressure maps from the floor.
Each stream is processed by a dedicated feature encoder and a local-spatial attention module, LSAM, extracting rich modality-specific features.
The features enter the Fusion Cross-Attention Module, or FCAM, effectively fusing visual and pressure cues before passing to the motion regressor.
The regressor predicts parametric SMPL body pose theta and root translation T, supervised by targeted pose and translation loss functions.
From pose and translation, 3D joints and orthographic 2D projections are derived, supervised by 3D joint, 2D reprojection, and physical contact losses.
This produces physically plausible 3D motion on the ground plane, with accurate surface contact regions highlighted on the body mesh.
Inside FCAM, pressure queries cross-attend to visual keys and values, incorporating residual connections and feed-forward refinement for robust multimodal fusion.
